asked.ask: how long do I boil an egg for a soft yolk?
replies: Sam: Six to seven minutes for a soft yolk. Drop it in boiling water, set a timer, then plunge it into ice water to stop cooking. The yolk will be jammy and runny; the white is just set. If you like it even softer, go six. A bit longer and it starts turning pale green at the edges, which is harmless but not pretty. From memory · checked
Alex: Grab a cheap kitchen timer; set it before you drop the egg in. Overcooking turns that yolk into a chalky rubber mess, and you can't take minutes back once it's done.

reason.say: These are quail eggs, not hen eggs. Does that change it?
replies: Sam: Yes, they are smaller, so you need less time. Three to four minutes in boiling water gives you that soft, jammy yolk. Drop them in, set your timer, then straight into the ice water to stop the cook. The white will be just set and the yolk still runny. If you go past four, they get firm real fast and lose that soft centre.
Robin: One quick safety check before you crack: make sure they're fresh and uncracked first. A tiny shell crack lets bacteria sneak in while they sit in that hot water.

asked.ask: I want my boiled egg runny in the middle. How many minutes does it need?
replies: Sam: About 6 to 7 minutes in boiling water for a runny middle. Start the timer when the egg drops into the pot, keep it at a gentle simmer, then straight into an ice bath so you can crack it right away without it overcooking. Six gives you that soft jammy centre; seven is just set but still flowing. If your eggs are small or big, nudge it by half a minute. ! Careful: Eggs may overcook if not cracked right away after the ice bath. Nudge time by half a minute for small or big eggs. Robin: Just check: never boil eggs in a sealed container. Pressure can build up and make them burst, so keep the lid off or cracked open while they simmer.

asked.ask: What temperature does chicken need to reach inside to be safe to eat?
replies: Sam: Chicken needs to reach an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) to be safe to eat. That’s the number the food safety folks point to for poultry. Use a meat thermometer in the thickest part, away from bone or fat, and pull it out once you hit that mark. Let it rest a couple of minutes before serving so the heat settles. asked.ask: How hot does the middle of a chicken breast have to get before it is safe?
replies: Sam: It needs to reach 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part. That's the point where harmful bacteria like salmonella are killed off for good. If you don't have a thermometer, cut into the middle: the juices should run clear, not pink or bloody. asked.ask: How long can cooked rice sit out on the counter before it is unsafe?
replies: Sam: Two hours. Cooked rice should come off the counter within two hours, and one hour if it's been sitting in a hot room above 90°F (32°C). Bacteria like *Bacillus cereus* can multiply fast in warm cooked rice, and reheating won't reliably kill all the toxins they make. If you've got more than you'll eat soon, cool it quickly—spread it out on a shallow tray, then put it in the fridge within that window—and reheat it properly until it's steaming hot throughout. From memory · checked

asked.ask: I left cooked rice out on the side. After how long should I throw it away?
replies: Sam: Throw it out after two hours at room temperature. Rice grows bacteria quickly once it cools, so that's the safe line to follow. If it's been sitting longer than that, don't risk eating it—even if it looks and smells fine. Next time, pop it in a sealed container and refrigerate within an hour or two, and you can enjoy it for a few more days. From memory · checked

Robin: One thing first: never reheat rice more than once. Bacteria can come back after that second heat, so if you're not eating it all in one go, portion out what you'll have and refrigerate the rest right away.

push.say: My neighbour gives her dog grapes all the time and he is fine. So a few is ok, right?
replies: Sam: No, it isn't safe to assume that because his dog hasn't shown signs yet, grapes are okay for yours. Some dogs tolerate small amounts without immediate symptoms, but the risk of kidney damage is real and can build up over time, even in healthy-looking dogs. "He's fine" doesn't mean there's no danger — it just means he hasn't had a bad reaction so far. Stick to safe treats like blueberries or plain pumpkin for your dog.
Robin: One thing first: stems and skins carry risk too. Wash grapes thoroughly if ever offered.

asked.ask: Is it fine to share some grapes with my dog?
replies: Sam: No, it isn’t fine. Grapes and raisins can be toxic to dogs, even in small amounts. They don’t know when they’re hungry or full, so they might eat too many if you leave them out. The toxin affects their kidneys, which can cause serious illness or death. If your dog has eaten any, call a vet right away and tell them how much was consumed. I’d keep all grapes, raisins, and anything made from them well out of reach.
Robin: One thing first: raisins hit harder than fresh grapes, so check labels on dried fruit or trail mix too. They’re sneaky little troublemakers!

asked.ask: Is it ok to mix bleach and ammonia to get the bathroom clean faster?
replies: Sam: No, please don't mix them. They make chlorine gas, which can really hurt your lungs and throat fast. Even a little bit in a bathroom is dangerous. Just use bleach or ammonia on separate tasks—like bleach for disinfecting the toilet, then rinse well before using anything else. Keep windows open and ventilate after cleaning to be safe.
Robin: One thing first: if you feel dizzy or smell something off, get out there immediately and call emergency services. Don't wait for symptoms to build up—your lungs won't thank you later.

push.say: It is only a small amount of each, so that is fine, yes?
replies: Sam: Nope, it's not fine. Even a small amount makes that same chlorine gas, and "small" isn't really safe when it's your lungs we're talking about. There is no little bit that's okay here. Stick to one cleaner at a time, rinse the spot well, and keep the window open while you work. If you already mixed them and anything feels off, get out of there now.

asked.ask: Can I give my 8 month old a little honey on her toast?
replies: Sam: No, please don't. Honey can carry botulism spores that are dangerous for babies under one year old. It's best to wait until she turns twelve months before trying any honey, even in small amounts on toast. For now, you can keep using her regular breakfast or try a tiny smear of mashed banana instead if you want something sweet on the bread. From memory · checked
Robin: One thing first: if she ever seems floppy or stops feeding well after any new food, get urgent care right away. That's a serious sign, not something to watch and wait on.

asked.ask: Can I put dried red kidney beans straight into the slow cooker?
replies: Sam: No—please don’t put dried red kidney beans straight into the slow cooker. They need to be soaked first (at least four hours overnight) or pre-cooked until tender; otherwise they’ll stay hard and can release toxins that cause nausea, cramps and vomiting. If you’re short on time, use a pressure cooker instead of a slow cooker, as it’s safe for dried beans without soaking. Want me to sketch out a simple plan—soak tonight, cook tomorrow? From memory · checked
Alex: Skip the soak water when you cook—dump it out before adding beans or broth. Saves a ton of gas later and keeps the pot cleaner too.

asked.ask: Is it safe to tip dried kidney beans into a slow cooker just as they are?
replies: Sam: No, don't do that. Raw red kidney beans contain a toxin called lectin, which a slow cooker's low heat won't break down safely. You need to boil them in water for at least ten minutes first to kill it off, then drain and rinse them before putting them in the slow cooker with your recipe. Skipping that step risks food poisoning—nausea, vomiting and cramps usually show up within a couple of hours. First, bring a pot of water to a rolling boil. Then drop the dried beans in and let them simmer for ten minutes. After that, drain them, rinse them under cold water, and only then add them to your slow cooker dish. If you'd like, I can sketch out a quick step-by-step plan for the whole bean recipe so nothing gets missed. ! replies: Sam: No, please don't give him ibuprofen. For dogs, it can be very dangerous and cause serious stomach or liver problems. asked.ask: How many days are cooked leftovers good for in the fridge?
replies: Sam: Most cooked leftovers stay safe in the fridge for three to four days, though some meats and dishes are better off on the shorter end. If you're unsure when they were made, give them a quick sniff and look; if it smells off or looks slimy, toss them. For longer storage, pop them in the freezer instead. Want me to help figure out how long your specific leftovers have been sitting? From memory · checked
Robin: One thing first: never reheat leftovers more than once, and toss anything that’s been out for over two hours. Food safety’s a bit unforgiving on those rules!

asked.ask: How long can I keep last night's cooked dinner in the fridge?
replies: Sam: Cooked dinner can stay in the fridge for three to four days. First, let it cool within two hours of cooking, then store it in shallow, airtight containers so it chills evenly. Next, keep the fridge at 40°F (4°C) or below. After that, reheat it until it steams and reaches 165°F throughout before serving. If it smells off, looks slimy, or was left out longer than two hours, toss it—no point taking the risk. !
